paragraphs: 4 former Mustangs appeared in professional games on Thursday for 4 clubs across 2 levels, with Ryan Tayman producing the night's most notable performance.
Ryan Tayman's home run — his 2th of the season came in the second inning on a 0-1 pitch from Iker Redona. The swing moved the score from 0-0 to 1-0.
Ryan Tayman went 1-for-3, 1 home run, 1 RBI, 1 run scored.
He batted sixth and started behind the plate.
St. Lucie Mets fell to Daytona Tortugas, 2-8.

Alejandro Garza went 2-for-4, 1 triple, 1 RBI, 1 run scored, 1 walk for Hill City Howlers at Single-A. Alejandro Garza put his club in front in the first with a go-ahead triple to right field on a 2-1 pitch from Gabe Tanner, changing the score from 0-0 to 2-0. He batted second and started at designated hitter. Hill City Howlers beat Kannapolis Cannon Ballers, 7-6.

Tanner Sagouspe came on in relief for Fresno Grizzlies in the bottom of the eighth with nobody out. He worked 1.0 innings, allowing 0 hits and 0 earned runs, striking out 3 without issuing a walk. One of his strikeouts came in the eighth on a 2-2 pitch, when he put away Grant Jay. Fresno Grizzlies fell to Inland Empire 66ers, 2-8.

Steven Brooks started on the mound for Portland Sea Dogs. He worked 2.0 innings, allowing 2 hits and 1 earned run, with 2 walks and 1 strikeout. One of his strikeouts came in the second on a 2-2 pitch, when he put away Jack Payton. Portland Sea Dogs beat Richmond Flying Squirrels, 11-2.

paragraphs: 6 former Mustangs appeared in professional games on Wednesday for 6 clubs across 3 levels, with Brooks Lee producing the night's most notable performance.

Brooks Lee went 1-for-4, 1 home run, 1 RBI, 1 run scored.
He batted second and started at third base.
Minnesota Twins fell to Athletics, 4-7.

One of his strikeouts came in the sixth on a 1-2 pitch, when he put away Aidan Smith. Hudson Valley Renegades fell to Brooklyn Cyclones, 5-11.
Alejandro Garza went 1-for-4, 1 stolen base for Hill City Howlers at Single-A. He batted first and started at second base. Hill City Howlers fell to Kannapolis Cannon Ballers, 0-5.

Taylor Dollard started on the mound for Everett AquaSox. He worked 1 1/3 innings, allowing 0 hits and 0 earned runs, with 1 walk and 1 strikeout. One of his strikeouts came in the first on a 1-2 pitch, when he put away Cam Maldonado. Everett AquaSox beat Eugene Emeralds, 11-6.
Ryan Stafford went 1-for-1 for Frederick Keys at High-A. He batted ninth and appeared at PH. Frederick Keys beat Asheville Tourists, 3-2.

Bryan Woo started on the mound for Seattle Mariners. He worked 4.0 innings, allowing 5 hits and 6 earned runs, with 1 walk and 5 strikeouts. One of his strikeouts came in the first on a 0-2 98 mph four-seam fastball, when he put away Trea Turner. Seattle Mariners fell to Philadelphia Phillies, 0-6.

paragraphs: 7 former Mustangs appeared in professional games on Tuesday for 7 clubs across 4 levels, with Alejandro Garza producing the night's most notable performance.
Alejandro Garza produced a double in the fifth to right field on the first pitch from Blaine Wynk.

Hill City Howlers beat Kannapolis Cannon Ballers, 7-6.

Andrew Alvarez started on the mound for Washington Nationals. He worked 4 2/3 innings, allowing 5 hits and 3 earned runs, with 2 walks and 6 strikeouts. One of his strikeouts came in the third on a 2-2 93 mph sinker, when he put away Jake McCarthy. Washington Nationals fell to Colorado Rockies, 1-3.

Drew Thorpe started on the mound for Charlotte Knights. He worked 4 2/3 innings, allowing 6 hits and 2 earned runs, with 1 walk and 3 strikeouts. One of his strikeouts came in the first on a 1-2 81 mph changeup, when he put away Colton Ledbetter. Charlotte Knights beat Memphis Redbirds, 8-2.

Brooks Lee went 1-for-4, 1 double for Minnesota Twins. Brooks Lee produced a double in the seventh to right field on a 0-1 95 mph four-seam fastball from Hogan Harris. He batted seventh and started at third base. Minnesota Twins fell to Athletics, 2-4.
Zach Daudet went 1-for-4 for Asheville Tourists at High-A. He batted sixth and started at shortstop. Asheville Tourists fell to Frederick Keys, 3-6.
Ryan Tayman went 0-for-4, 1 run scored, 2 walks for St. Lucie Mets at Single-A. He batted third and started at designated hitter. St. Lucie Mets beat Daytona Tortugas, 12-5.
Ryan Stafford went 0-for-2 for Frederick Keys at High-A. He batted eighth and started behind the plate. Frederick Keys beat Asheville Tourists, 6-3.
